newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOING TO SYDNEY OLYMPICS? PRAY FOR GOOD WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: GOING TO SYDNEY OLYMPICS? PRAY FOR GOOD WEATHER.

text.p: If you are planning a trip to the Sydney 2000 Olympics, pray that the weather is good, otherwise you could be in for a three hour bus ride to the city.

Sydney airport owner, the Federal Airports Corp, on Thursday said a contingency plan was in place to divert aircraft to the Australian capital Canberra, 300 km (180 miles) to the southwest, if the city's airport was forced to close due to bad weather.
Travellers would then be bussed to Sydney.
However, the upside is that Sydney airport rarely closes, except when coastal fog smothers it.
Moreover, the 2000 Games will be held between September 15 and October 1, during the southern hemisphere spring, avoiding Australia's sweltering summer heat.
"Statistically, September is supposed to be the driest month, so I think our chances are very low, but it (closure) could happen," the airport's chief executive Barry Murphy told reporters.
Strong winds could also lead to diversions.

"If we were unlucky enough to get sustained strong westerly winds for long periods that could reduce the runway to perhaps 40 movements per hour...then that is going to cause us some headaches," Murphy said.
Sydney airport is restricted by law to 80 aircraft movements per hour and a night curfew.
